title: Classify code-search snippets and path metadata as source-sensitive
description:
Problem: code-search results are exposed as generic read-only data even though they can contain source snippets, local file paths, repository metadata, index metadata, line ranges, and other filesystem details.

Desired outcome: code-search disclosure matches the source-sensitivity model and does not expose local layout or excerpts to callers without explicit permission.

Scope:
- Reclassify source-bearing search results as source-sensitive, or split metadata-only and source-result tools.
- Remove absolute paths, repository roots, and index paths from ordinary responses.
- Preserve useful metadata-only search for callers that lack source-read capability.
- Add authorization and response-shape regression tests for chat and MCP.
- Out of scope: changing ranking or vector-storage performance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ordinary read-only callers cannot retrieve source snippets or local filesystem paths.
- Explicit source-read callers receive only the bounded fields they are authorized to see.
- Tool descriptors, documentation, and policy checks agree on the sensitivity level.
- Tests cover anonymous, viewer, source-read, editor, and administrator contexts.

Validation:
- Run focused code-search and MCP authorization tests.
- Run the retrieval validation suite.
- Run Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.
